standard.title: Develop questions to guide investigations
standard.description: develop questions to guide investigations about people, events, places and issues
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2S01): Students developed inquiry questions about historical sites and places using factual and perspective-seeking stems.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop questions to guide investigations about people, events, places and issues, including consequential and ethical questions.

nodes.label: Expanded question types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a range of question types including 'Why there?' location questions, 'What might happen?' consequence questions, and 'What ought to happen?' ethical questions.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least three questions of different types (location, consequence, ethical or comparative) about a HASS topic.
nodes.typical_width: Develop inquiring questions including: 'Why there?' about location; 'What might happen?' about consequences; 'What ought to happen?' about ethics; 'How have things changed?' comparative questions; probing questions during investigation.
wider: Evaluate a set of student-generated questions for a HASS investigation by type and usefulness and revise the least useful ones
Generate questions that could be investigated using different inquiry methods (fieldwork, interview, documentary analysis) and discuss which method suits each question
nodes.hinge_reason: Consequential and ethical question types are new at Year 3 and are required for the civics and evaluating demands of the curriculum — without them, inquiry stays factual.

response_modes.reason: Ethical and consequential question types require explicit modelling — students need examples and practice before generating these independently.

success_criteria: Develops at least three questions of different types
At least one question goes beyond factual recall to consequence or ethics
